C1.wording: No REQ change; feedback incorporation is routine coordination
C1.rationale: The statement describes folding received feedback into existing work and flagging unverified items. This reads as a general quality habit applied across deliverables rather than a distinct recurring deliverable, so it may not warrant a requirement.

C1.wording: Validated findings, incorporating feedback with unverified items flagged
C1.rationale: Noting where feedback has not yet been checked is closely tied to validation status. Widening the validated-findings task would capture tracking of verified versus unverified inputs without adding a new task.

C1.wording: Feedback incorporation log with verification status
C1.rationale: If stakeholder feedback recurs across deliverables and its verification status matters, a small dedicated task could make that tracking an explicit deliverable. This is weaker given only one distinct statement in the cluster.

C2.rationale: A single statement from one employee describes informal peer cross-checking before a handoff. This is coordination or one-off quality practice rather than a distinct deliverable, so it should not become a requirement.

If cross-checking results is a routine part of validating findings, the existing Validated findings task could be worded to include peer verification. The evidence is thin, with one statement from one employee.
The statement already aligns to the Assessment report task under SIM-TTO-1-03. Comparing results before a write-up may belong to that existing task rather than to this REQ.

C3.wording: No REQ change; clarification edits are incidental
C3.rationale: A single statement from one employee describes adding clarifying examples to a description. This reads as ordinary quality work on existing deliverables, not a recurring distinct requirement.
If the clarified descriptions are vulnerability findings, adding illustrative examples could fall within producing validated findings. A narrow wording change would cover it without a new task.
The statement already aligns to the Executive briefing task on SIM-TTO-1-02. Clarifying descriptions with examples for an audience fits briefing work, so it may be covered there.
